title: Date arithmetic
description:
Write date helpers that work on plain year, month and day numbers, using `mktime` for the hard part:

```c
int add_days(int *year, int *month, int *day, int days);         /* moves the date; 0, or -1 if mktime fails */
long days_between(int y1, int m1, int d1, int y2, int m2, int d2);   /* second date minus first, in whole days */
int last_day_of_month(int year, int month);                      /* 28 to 31 */
```

- Work at noon (`tm_hour = 12`, `tm_isdst = -1`), so daylight saving never changes the date.
- `days_between` uses `difftime` and rounds to the nearest whole day (a day with a clock change is 23 or 25 hours long).
- `last_day_of_month` asks for "day 0 of the next month", which `mktime` turns into the last day of this one.
hints: One helper that fills a `struct tm` at noon and calls `mktime` serves all three functions (lesson 8.03).
Day 0 of a month is the day before day 1, which is the last day of the month before: `mktime` works it out.
